title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 79
paragraphs: So when they had killed the Magians and cut off their heads, they left behind those of their number who were wounded, both because these were unable to go and to take charge of the fortress. The other five, taking the heads of the Magians with them, ran with shouting and the clashing of arms and called on the other Persians to join them, telling what had been done and showing the heads. At the same time they killed every Magian who crossed their path. When the Persians heard what the seven had brought about and of the Magians' deception, they too decided to do the same, and drawing their daggers they killed every Magian they found. Had night not come on and stopped them, they would not have left a single Magian alive. This day the Persians celebrate in common more than any other day, and on it they keep a great festival which they call the Festival of the Slaughter of the Magians. On this day no Magian is permitted to appear out of doors, and the Magians keep themselves within their houses throughout that day.
